A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the U62A variant is a snapshot of the structure of the wild-type U6 snRnP core, but the wild-type ISl is dynamic and can adopt different conformations.
the U6 snRNA ISL is inherently dynamic and that the Prp24 core structure is robust and adaptable to accommodate this conformational flexibility.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Prp24-U6 complex has the ability to adopt two different conformations, one of which may be relevant to its function in vivo.

the structure of the U4/U6 di-snRNP is not a simple combination of the two individual snRNAs, but rather that their pairing is accompanied by substantial rearrangements in the conformation and topology of the U6 ISL.

the U6 snRNPs crystallized in two different space groups exhibit similar structures, suggesting that they are not trapped in a crystallographic `crystallographic artifact' and are likely to be biologically relevant.
